dialogue_quality_notes: Concise, workplace-appropriate negotiation: rule stated, concern raised, quick accommodation offered.
One explicit accommodation formula ('If your sleeve covers it completely, that works.') resolved the dispute cleanly.
Minor unnecessary repetition of the settled line in round 12 ('If your sleeve covers it completely...').
evaluation.final_reason: Agent A accepted a practical accommodation: 'If your sleeve covers it completely, that works.' Agent D agreed to that condition: 'Okay. I'll make sure it stays covered.' Thus the substantive incompatibility (store rule banning visible accessories vs D's religious bracelet) was resolved when A permitted the bracelet so long as it was fully covered and D agreed to keep it covered.

Agent A moved from enforcing the rule strictly to allowing a specific accommodation ('If your sleeve covers it completely, that works.').
Agents B and C remained supportive of complying with the rule and did not change position.

Local agreement can be reached without head office input by interpreting 'visible' as the operative constraint.
